Microcausality ([ϕ(x),ϕ(y)]=0 for spacelike x−y)

Words: 145 Articles: 1
Relativistic quantum field OurBigBook.com
Microcausality requires local bosonic observables at spacelike separation to commute. For a free real scalar field, the field commutator is the difference of its two Wightman functions; it vanishes at equal time and, by Lorentz invariance, at every spacelike separation. Nonzero spacelike vacuum correlations do not violate this condition, since a correlation is different from the response to a local intervention. Odd fermionic fields satisfy a corresponding spacelike anticommutation condition, while physical even local observables commute.

Antiparticle modes and spacelike commutativity

Words: 75
Microcausality OurBigBook.com
For a free complex scalar field, independent particle annihilators and antiparticle creators give
[Φ(x),Φ†(y)]=∫(2π)32Ep​d3p​(e−ip(x−y)−eip(x−y)).
(1)
The invariant mass shell integral vanishes at spacelike separation: transform to equal time, then reverse the spatial momentum in one term. Retaining only the particle-annihilation term would leave a Wightman function, which is generally nonzero even at spacelike separation. Thus both frequency branches are needed for a local relativistic field. For a real scalar field, the creation term supplies the same cancellation but creates the same self-conjugate particle species.

Massive spin-two field ((□−m2)hmn​=0,∂mhmn​=0,hmm​=0)

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Relativistic quantum field OurBigBook.com
A free massive spin-two field is a symmetric tensor obeying a massive Klein-Gordon equation, vanishing divergence, and vanishing trace. Its rest-frame polarizations form the symmetric traceless square of the SO(D−1) vector, with (D−2)(D+1)/2 degrees of freedom.

Light-cone decomposition of a massive spin-two field (Sym02​(RD−1)↓SO(D−2)=Sym02​(RD−2)⊕RD−2⊕R)

Words: 32
Massive spin-two field OurBigBook.com
When ∂−​ is invertible, divergence determines components with a plus index from h−−​,h−I​,hIJ​. The trace constraint fixes the trace of hIJ​. The remaining transverse group representations are a symmetric traceless square, a vector representation, and a scalar.

Decay width (Γ)

Relativistic quantum field OurBigBook.com
In units with ℏ=1, the inverse lifetime of an unstable particle. A neutral meson mixing effective Hamiltonian operator incorporates decay through its anti-Hermitian part −iΓ/2.

Branching fraction (Bi​=Γi​/Γtot​)

Words: 40
Decay width OurBigBook.com
A branching fraction is the probability that a decay occurs through a particular mutually exclusive channel, equal to its partial decay width divided by the total decay width. Inclusive channel fractions sum to one. Rounding displayed fractions can make their numerical sum differ from one.

Decay amplitude (M(i→f))

Words: 148 Articles: 1
Decay width OurBigBook.com
The invariant decay amplitude is the transition matrix element for one incoming particle and a specified on-shell final state, with the overall momentum delta function factored out. For covariantly normalized states, write the connected S-matrix element as i(2π)4δ4(pi​−pf​)M(i→f). Its overall phase does not affect the decay width. The rate is Γ=(2Mi​)−1∑spins​∫dΦf​∣M∣2, with the initial spin average included when the initial state is unpolarized. For a spin-zero parent and an angle-independent two-body amplitude, the two-body Lorentz-invariant phase space gives Γ=∣k∣∑∣M∣2/(8πMi2​). In leptonic pion decay, contracting the axial hadronic matrix element with the chiral weak charged current makes this amplitude proportional to the charged-lepton mass, proving helicity suppression.

Absorptive phase of a decay amplitude (δ)

Words: 43
Decay amplitude OurBigBook.com
An absorptive phase arises from physical intermediate states or rescattering in a decay amplitude. For a pair of CP symmetry conjugate reactions with otherwise symmetric dynamics, this phase is the same in both amplitudes, whereas a weak phase changes sign. Their differing transformation laws allow interference to produce a direct CP asymmetry.

Massive-vector spin average (∣M∣2​=31​∑spins​∣M∣2)

Words: 53
Decay width OurBigBook.com
An unpolarized decay of a massive spin-one particle averages the squared amplitude over three parent spin states. Its polarization sum is −ημν​+pμ​pν​/m2. For a conserved external current the longitudinal pμ​pν​ term drops out, but this does not replace the spin average by 1/2: the physical massive parent still has three states.

Massless semileptonic pseudoscalar decay rate (dΓ/ds=GF2​∣V∣2λ3/2∣f+​(s)∣2/(192π3M3))

Words: 77
Decay width OurBigBook.com
For a pseudoscalar meson of mass M decaying into a pseudoscalar meson of mass m and two massless leptons through a weak charged current, the transverse massless leptonic current selects f+​(s). With hadronic current normalized as (p+k)μf+​(s)+(p−k)μf−​(s) and flavour coefficient V,
dsdΓ​=192π3M3GF2​∣V∣2​λ(s,M2,m2)3/2∣f+​(s)∣2,0≤s≤(M−m)2.
(2)
The Källén function has mass dimension four, and the coefficient has mass dimension −7. This decay rate assumes the stated form-factor normalization and no additional isospin factor. It follows by the integrated massless leptonic tensor and the pion momentum change of variable in the parent's centre-of-momentum frame.

Lorentz-invariant phase space (dΦ2​)

Words: 125 Articles: 2
Decay width OurBigBook.com
For two outgoing particles the Lorentz-invariant phase space is dΦ2​=(2π)4δ(4)(p−k−k′)d3k/((2π)32Ek​)d3k′/((2π)32Ek′​). With massless daughters in their center-of-mass frame, dΦ2​=dΩ/(32π2) and ∫dΦ2​=1/(8π). This fixes normalization factors in decay widths and scattering rates.

Two-body Lorentz-invariant phase space (dΦ2​=dΩ/(32π2))

Words: 97 Articles: 1
Lorentz-invariant phase space OurBigBook.com
For two distinct massless final particles in their centre-of-momentum frame, integrating the energy-momentum delta function gives dΦ2​=dΩ/(32π2). A massless two-particle initial state has flux 2s, hence dσ/dcosθ=∣M∣2​/(32πs). Average only over the initial spin states physically present.
Massless two-body scattering flux normalization (dσ/dΩ=∣M∣2​/(64π2s))
Words: 56
Two-body Lorentz-invariant phase space OurBigBook.com
For two distinct massless final particles, dΦ2​/dΩ=1/(32π2) in the centre-of-mass frame. The invariant initial flux is 4p1​⋅p2​=2s. Their ratio gives the displayed differential cross-section. Equivalently the denominator is 128π2p1​⋅p2​. Initial spins are averaged and final spins and colors summed when defining an inclusive unpolarized cross-section; averaging final colors would change the observable.

Polarization vector (εμ(p,λ))

Words: 198 Articles: 4
Relativistic quantum field OurBigBook.com
A Lorentz four-vector coefficient selecting a spin-one polarization in a mode expansion of a free field. Its allowed components depend on the field equations and gauge fixing.

Longitudinal polarization of a massive vector boson (εLμ​)

Words: 40
Polarization vector OurBigBook.com
A physical polarization of a massive spin-one gauge boson whose spatial polarization points along its spatial momentum. Together with two transverse polarizations it supplies the three physical spin states. In the Higgs mechanism, a broken-direction Goldstone boson supplies this extra state as the gauge boson acquires mass.

Photon polarization completeness relation (∑r​ϵi(r)​ϵj(r)∗​=δij​−ki​kj​/∣k∣2)

Words: 34
Polarization vector OurBigBook.com
Two orthonormal transverse polarization vectors span the plane perpendicular to a nonzero momentum. Summing their dyadic products gives the spatial transverse projector. It has trace and rank two and acts as the identity on physical photon polarizations.

Polarization sum for a massive vector boson (∑λ​ϵμ​(k,λ)ϵν∗​(k,λ)=−gμν​+kμ​kν​/m2)

Words: 52
Polarization vector OurBigBook.com
For m>0, the three physical polarization vectors are transverse to k and have norm −1 in metric (+−−−). In the rest frame their sum is diag(0,1,1,1); Lorentz covariance then gives the displayed expression for k2=m2. This includes the longitudinal mode. It cannot be specialized to m=0 by setting its denominator to zero.

Timelike photon polarization (ϵ0μ=(1,0,0,0))

Words: 53
Polarization vector OurBigBook.com
A timelike basis polarization in covariant photon quantization has positive Minkowski metric squared length, conventionally ϵ0μ=(1,0) with signature (+,−,−,−). It is distinct from the spatial longitudinal polarization ϵ3μ=(0,p​). The extra minus sign in the covariant oscillator commutator makes its one-photon state a negative-norm photon state. Neither this temporal polarization nor an isolated longitudinal photon survives the Gupta-Bleuler null-state quotient.

Fierz-Pauli equations

Relativistic quantum field OurBigBook.com
The Fierz-Pauli equations describe a free massive spin-two field. A symmetric tensor hμν​ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation together with ∂μhμν​=0 and hμμ​=0, leaving five propagating polarizations in four dimensions.

A free Dirac field has Lagrangian density L=iψˉ​γμ∂μ​ψ−mψˉ​ψ and obeys the Dirac equation.

Dirac fermion number conservation ([Q,S]=0)

Words: 88
Dirac field OurBigBook.com
A Dirac field theory invariant under ψ↦eiαψ, ψˉ​↦e−iαψˉ​ has a conserved global charge, subject to the quantum theory preserving the symmetry. In particle language this charge counts particles minus antiparticles. When the S-matrix commutes with it, a scattering amplitude between states of different charge vanishes. A neutral scalar and a Yukawa interaction preserve the charge, so a process with one incoming Dirac particle and only one outgoing Dirac antiparticle plus neutral particles is forbidden. This net charge is distinct from a sum of positive occupation numbers for all particle and antiparticle modes.

A local expression containing two fermion fields and a matrix acting on Dirac spinor indices. The choices Γ=γμ and Γ=γμγ5 give the Dirac current and axial current.

A fermion bilinear transforming as a Lorentz four-vector. For a single Dirac field this is the Dirac current; distinct flavours can give a charged or flavour-changing current.

Mode expansion of a Dirac field

Words: 298 Articles: 7
Dirac field OurBigBook.com
The mode expansion of a free Dirac field decomposes it into positive-frequency particle modes and negative-frequency antiparticle modes:
ψ(x)=∑s​∫dΠp​[bs(p)us(p)e−ip⋅x+ds†(p)vs(p)eip⋅x].
(3)
The operators bs and ds obey fermionic anticommutation relations.

Particle and antiparticle occupation operators of a Dirac field (Ntotal​=Ne​+Neˉ​,Q=Ne​−Neˉ​)

Words: 60
Mode expansion of a Dirac field OurBigBook.com
The positive occupation operators are Ne​=∑s​∫d3paps†​aps​/(2π)3 and Neˉ​=∑s​∫d3pbps†​bps​/(2π)3. Both commute with the free Hamiltonian. The normal-ordered local density integral ∫:ψ†ψ:d3x is their difference, not their sum. It generates the global phase symmetry. For electron charge −e, electric charge is −eQ. Pair creation can change total occupation while preserving this net charge.

Antiparticle

Words: 159 Articles: 3

Boundary variation of the Yang-Mills theta term (δ∫M​tr(F∧F)=2∫∂M​tr(δA∧F))
Words: 82
Yang-Mills theta term OurBigBook.com
For F=dA+A∧A, the gauge-theory Bianchi identity is DF=0 and the variation is δF=DδA. The graded product rule for the covariant exterior derivative gives the displayed boundary integral. Thus a constant-coefficient Yang-Mills theta term leaves the bulk Yang-Mills equations unchanged, but can change the boundary variational condition. Its four-form density is exactly gauge-invariant by conjugation of F and cyclicity of the matrix trace, even if the gauge parameter is nonzero on the boundary. Gauge changes of a local Chern-Simons 3-form must not be confused with gauge changes of this globally defined curvature density.
CP parity of the Yang-Mills theta density (ϵμνρσFμνa​Fρσa​)
Words: 59
Yang-Mills theta term OurBigBook.com
The color-contracted density ϵμνρσFμνa​Fρσa​ is even under charge conjugation and odd under parity. In matrix form the two charge-conjugation signs cancel and transposition leaves the trace of the product unchanged. Parity contributes its orientation-reversing determinant to the four-index Levi-Civita symbol. Thus the density is CP odd. A generic fixed coefficient violates CP symmetry; being a local total derivative does not eliminate effects from nontrivial gauge topology.

A nontrivial covariant BRST charge therefore acts before reduction on an indefinite-inner-product gauge/ghost space. Exact vectors are null and orthogonal to closed vectors, and BRST cohomology quotients them out. Positivity of the reduced physical space requires the additional gauge-theory structure; it does not follow from abstract nilpotence alone.

The FP ghost sector is part of the physical prescription.

For an admissible family of gauge-fixing fermions, variation inserts a BRST-exact operator into normalized correlations. If the measured operators are BRST-closed, the graded BRST Ward identity makes that insertion vanish. This extends gauge-parameter independence to changes of the gauge functional itself, provided the action and measure preserve BRST symmetry and the change produces no boundary contribution. It is the perturbative statement; global gauge-orbit problems require additional analysis.

An invariant path-integral measure and BRST symmetry action imply this identity when every separated insertion Gi​ is BRST-closed. BRST cohomology
Words: 211 Articles: 4
BRST symmetry OurBigBook.com
BRST cohomology identifies physical states and observables with BRST-closed objects modulo BRST-exact ones. A change of gauge-fixing fermion changes the action by a BRST-exact term and therefore leaves BRST-cohomology classes unchanged when the measure has no BRST anomaly.
Positive one-particle BRST cohomology ({ε:k⋅ε=0}/span{k})
Words: 94
BRST cohomology OurBigBook.com
For a nonzero null momentum and a nontrivial BRST charge on the gauge/ghost one-particle sector, closed vector states obey k⋅ε=0 and exact vector states have polarization proportional to k. The Faddeev-Popov ghost field state is exact and the antighost field state is not closed. With mostly-plus Minkowski metric, choose k=(ω,0,0,ω); closure sets ε3=ε0, so the norm is ∣ε1∣2+∣ε2∣2. Quotienting by the null longitudinal polarization leaves two positive-norm transverse polarizations per group index. Self-adjointness and nilpotence alone do not establish positivity on an arbitrary state space: the nonzero momentum, nontrivial charge and stated indefinite inner products are essential here.
